title: Push and pull factors

match.reason: The bank point is a Year 11 NSW card on migration as a whole, with more depth (weighing factors, costs, family ties) and examples such as Sudan and Sydney, so it is broader and at a different depth from the Year 8 push and pull factors point.

draft.title: Push and pull factors
card: People move from one place to another for reasons. Some of these reasons belong to the place they leave, and some to the place they go to.
something that drives people away from where they live, such as drought, few jobs or conflict.
something that draws people to a place, such as work, schools, health services or a safer home.
One move can have both. A family may be pushed out by drought on their farm and pulled to a town by a job offer.
draft.remember: Push factors are about the place people leave. Pull factors are about the place they move to.

a.q: A farm family leaves the land after three years of drought. Which factor pushed them?
opts: The drought on their farm
The schools in the nearby town
The jobs on offer in the city
The hospital in the regional centre
a.why: The drought is a problem at the place they left, so it drives them away. Schools, jobs and a hospital are features of other places that draw people in, so they are pull factors.
a.clue: Which reason is about the place they are leaving?

b.q: Priya leaves her small town in Western Australia because the only factory has closed. She moves to Perth, where she has been offered a job. Which statement is correct?
opts: The factory closure pushed her and the job pulled her
The factory closure pulled her and the job pushed her
Both reasons are push factors, as they led to her move
Both reasons are pull factors, as they led to her move
b.why: The closure is a problem in the place she left, so it is a push factor. The job is in Perth, the place she moved to, so it is a pull factor. Both led to her move, but a factor is sorted by which place it belongs to.
b.clue: Sort each reason by the place it belongs to.

b.best: The factory closure pushed her and the job pulled her

problems.detail: The stem says the family leaves 'after three years of drought', and the right option is 'The drought on their farm'. A student can match the word 'drought' without understanding push factors. None of the other options appear in the stem, which makes this too easy.

a.q: Sam's family lives on a cattle station and is thinking of moving to Darwin. Which of these would be a push factor for them?
opts: The station's nearest school closing down
A new high school opening in Darwin
Steady work on offer in Darwin
Friendly neighbours on nearby stations
a.why: The school closing is a problem at the place they live, so it drives them away. A new school and steady work in Darwin are features of the place they might move to, so they are pull factors. Friendly neighbours give them a reason to stay, not to leave.
a.clue: Which reason is a problem where they live now?

b.q: Priya leaves her small town in Western Australia because the only factory has closed. She moves to Perth, where she has been offered a job. Which statement is correct?

The factory closure pulled her and the job pushed her
Both reasons are push factors, as they led to her move
Both reasons are pull factors, as they led to her move
b.why: The closure is a problem in the place she left, so it is a push factor. The job is in Perth, the place she moved to, so it is a pull factor. Both led to her move, but a factor is sorted by which place it belongs to.
b.clue: Sort each reason by the place it belongs to.

b.best: The factory closure pushed her and the job pulled her
